meta.subject: Biology
meta.description: Seep Pahuja Biology - Chapter-wise DPP of selected Questions of NEET Biology

qs.q: Biosystematics aims at
o: The classification of organism based on their evolutionary history and establishing their phylogeny on the totality of various parameters from all fields of studies
Identification and arrangements of organism on the basis of their cytological characteristics
The classification of organisms based on broad morphological characters
Delimiting various taxa of organisms and establishing their relationships
qs.s: Biosystematics aims to classify organisms according to evolutionary relationships by incorporating parameters from genetics, cytology, anatomy, embryology, and ecology.

qs.q: Phenetic classification of organism is based on
o: The ancestral lineage of existing organism
qs.s: Phenetic classification (numerical taxonomy) evaluates overall similarity based entirely on observable morphological characteristics of existing organisms without considering evolutionary ancestry.

qs.q: ...A... is a collection of pressed, dried and preserved plants ...B... labelled arranged systematically for further reference. A and B in the above statement refers to
o: A-herbarium; B-mounted on a paper sheet
A-Museum; B-mounted on a iron sheet
A-Garden; B-mounted on a paper sheet
qs.s: A herbarium is a repository of plant specimens that are dried, pressed, and mounted on paper sheets with systematic labels for botanical reference.

qs.q: Arrange the following in the ascending order of Linnaean hierarchy.
qs.s: The ascending order of taxonomic categories starts from the most specific rank to the most inclusive: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom.

qs.q: Where was the first herbarium set up?
qs.s: The world's first herbarium was set up in Pisa, Italy, by Luca Ghini in the 16th century.

qs.q: Animal of the same phylum are grouped below. Choose the incorrect group from given below option
qs.s: Earthworm and leech belong to Phylum Annelida, whereas millipede belongs to Phylum Arthropoda. Thus, option 4 groups organisms from different phyla.

qs.q: Systematic botany means
o: Systematic arrangement of organs of plants
Systematic study of organelles and tissues
Methodical study of plants, dealing with identification, naming and classification
qs.s: Systematic botany encompasses the identification, nomenclature, and classification of plants taking into account their evolutionary relationships.

qs.q: What is the symbol of Bombay Natural History Society?
qs.s: The Great Hornbill (specifically 'William' the hornbill) is the official symbol and logo of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS).

qs.q: Which is called 'sexual system' of classification?
qs.s: Carolus Linnaeus devised the 'sexual system' of classification based primarily on numerical characteristics of floral reproductive organs (stamens and carpels).

qs.q: Identify from the following the only taxonomic category that has a real existence.
qs.s: Species is considered the only basic taxonomic rank with a real physical existence in nature as interbreeding biological populations.

qs.q: Process of metabolism leads to
qs.s: Metabolic reactions sustain life by driving growth, cell differentiation, development, and overall physiological functioning of the living body.

qs.q: Which of the following taxonomic ranks contain organism most similar to one another?
qs.s: Species is the lowest taxonomic rank, containing organisms that share the maximum number of common characters and can interbreed.

qs.q: Which is first step in taxonomy?
qs.s: Identification of an unknown organism is the prerequisite first step before it can be named (nomenclature) and categorized (classification).

qs.q: What is the prime source of taxonomic studies?
o: Collection of actual specimens of organisms species
Identification of actual specimen of organism species
qs.s: Taxonomic studies fundamentally depend on collecting actual specimens from the field and accurately identifying them.

qs.q: ... is a book (taxonomic aid) which contain information about habitat, distribution, climate description and index of plant found in a particular area
qs.s: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area, providing an index to the plant species occurring there.

qs.q: In hierarchical classification, class occupied a place between
qs.s: In the standard taxonomic hierarchy, Class is positioned directly below Phylum (or Division) and directly above Order.

qs.q: Select the correct option from the following
o: Worker bee undergoes reproduction to generate new progeny
Mule and worker bee do not reproduce
qs.s: Sterile organisms such as mules (interspecific hybrids) and worker bees (sterile females) are incapable of reproduction.

qs.q: Why hierarchical taxonomic system is used?
o: As each higher taxonomic category contains its below groups/categories
It is helpful to established classifications
All taxonomic categories reflect common habitats
Taxonomic group shows similar characters and have no evolutionary relationship
qs.s: A hierarchical system arranges taxa logically such that each higher rank encompasses one or more sub-ordinate lower groups.

qs.q: Biological organization in living state is at
qs.s: Biological organisation begins at the sub-microscopic molecular level, where inorganic and organic molecules interact to assemble organelles and living cellular systems.

qs.q:
Arrange the following in ascending similar characteristic
I. Family  II. Genus  III. Class  IV. Species
qs.s: Degree of similarity among members increases as we move down the taxonomic hierarchy. Thus, ascending order of similarity is Class < Family < Genus < Species.

qs.q:
Among the following choose the properties shown by the living organism exclusively?
I. growth  II. increase in mass  III. self-replication ability  IV. response to touch stimuli
qs.s: Intrinsic growth (I), self-replication (III), and responsiveness/consciousness (IV) are defining exclusive properties of living organisms. Non-living objects can accumulate mass externally.

qs.q: Which one of the following feature is shared by all living organism at all hierarchical level
qs.s: All living organisms across all taxonomic categories share fundamental biomolecular protoplasmic composition (proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, carbohydrates).

qs.q: ...A... is a collection of pressed, dried and preserved plants ...B... labelled arranged systematically for further reference. A and B in the above statement refers to
o: A-herbarium; B-mounted on a paper sheet
A-Museum; B-mounted on a iron sheet
A-Garden; B-mounted on a paper sheet
qs.s: A herbarium consists of pressed and dried plant specimens mounted on standard herbarium paper sheets.

qs.q: By which chemical specimen for herbaria are treated to prevent fungal attack
qs.s: Herbarium sheets and dried specimens are treated with 0.1\% mercuric chloride (HgCl_2) solution as a fungicide to prevent fungal damage.

qs.q: Who proposed binomial system of nomenclature?
qs.s: Carolus Linnaeus established and popularized the binomial system of nomenclature in his publication 'Species Plantarum' (1753).

qs.q: Term 'Taxonomy' was coined by
qs.s: A. P. de Candolle coined the term 'Taxonomy' in 1813 in his book 'Théorie Élémentaire de la Botanique'.

qs.q: A group of interconnected genera is called a
qs.s: Family is a taxonomic rank grouping together related genera that share common vegetative and reproductive characteristics.

qs.q: True regeneration is found in
qs.s: Planaria (flatworms) exhibits remarkable true regeneration, where a fragmented body part regenerates the entire organism.

qs.q:
Select true statement from the following and choose the right answer from the option given below
I. Human's scientific name is Homo sapiens
II. Genera Plantarum is written by John Ray
III. Highest taxonomic categories is division
IV. Taxonomic group of any rank is taxon
V. A group of closely related species of organism represent genus
VI. The term 'systematic' was coined by de Candolle
qs.s: Statements I, IV, and V are true. Genera Plantarum was written by Bentham & Hooker (and Linnaeus); Kingdom is the highest category; Linnaeus introduced the term 'Systematics'.

qs.q: Third name in trinomial nomenclature indicate
qs.s: In trinomial nomenclature, the third term specifies the sub-species (for animals) or variety (for plants).

qs.q: Who first proved that virus was made up of a nucleic acid and protein?
o: Dr Salvador Huria and Dr Max Delbruk
Dr NW Pirie and Dr FC Bawden
qs.s: Bawden and Pirie (1936) first demonstrated that viruses are nucleoproteins containing nucleic acids and protein components.

qs.q: The suffix 'phyta' indicates
qs.s: In plant taxonomy, the suffix '-phyta' is standardized under ICBN to designate a Division rank (e.g., Bryophyta, Spermatophyta).

qs.q: The genus Felis includes
qs.s: The genus Felis includes small cats (e.g., domestic cat Felis catus), whereas tigers belong to the genus Panthera.

qs.q: Who proposed binomial system of nomenclature?
qs.s: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature to provide a uniform two-word naming system for organisms.

qs.q: Where was the first herbarium set up?
qs.s: The first historic herbarium was created in Pisa, Italy, by botanical professor Luca Ghini.

qs.q: A group of organisms with similar trait of any rank is
qs.s: Taxon is a general term defined as a taxonomic group or unit of any rank in a biological classification system.

qs.q: Term 'New Systematics' was given by
qs.s: Julian Huxley proposed the term 'New Systematics' (Biosystematics) in 1940 to incorporate evolutionary, ecological, and genetic data into taxonomy.

qs.q: A genus with a single species is called
qs.s: A genus that comprises only one single species is designated as a monotypic genus.

qs.q: MABP stands for
o: Man and Biosphere Conservation and Protection
qs.s: MABP stands for UNESCO's 'Man and Biosphere Programme', launched to promote sustainable development and conservation.

qs.q: Which of the following is correctly sequenced?
qs.s: The correct descending taxonomic sequence is Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family.

qs.q: Choose the correct classification for the given plant
qs.s: The plant shows flowers (Angiosperm) with reticulate leaf venation, placing it under Dicotyledons of Kingdom Plantae.

qs.q: Choose the correct classification for the given plant
qs.s: The illustrated plant possesses flowers and reticulate leaf venation, identifying it as an Angiosperm Dicotyledon under Plantae.
